reel.caption:
₹5,000 SIP: what does a 10% yearly step-up do?

Illustrative, at an assumed 12% a year for 20 years:
Flat ₹5,000 a month → about ₹49.5 lakh (you put in ₹12 lakh).
Raise it 10% every year → about ₹98.5 lakh (you put in about ₹34.4 lakh).
Most of the gap is extra money in, plus more time for it to compound. Returns are not guaranteed and can be lower.

Would you rather step up your SIP or start a second one?

Sources: illustrative compounding maths; no real fund or return assumed.
